name: Prize crossword No 26,531
preamble: Five across clues lead to the names, not further defined, of the working partners of entertainers in the same line of business.

clue.text: See 17
Indianan mostly more difficult to please

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so one letter of the phrase's word is dropped, here its first

blocks.note: a choosy person is hard to please; this is the comparative

explanation.surface: Someone from Indiana is pickier than most.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOOSIER loses its C. 'Mostly' usually cuts the last letter; here it is the first that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoosier is the long-established nickname for a native or resident of the US state of Indiana.

clue.text: Get stuck quite often by the main gates

definitions.text: quite often by the main gates

blocks.note: first meaning: to become fixed or wedged somewhere, as a bone in the throat

blocks.clueFragment: quite often by the main gates
blocks.note: second meaning: the gatekeeper's house at the entrance to an estate, often found beside the gates

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a description rather than a synonym, which the blogger called a bit loose; 'quite often' hedges because not every one stands there.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means become firmly fixed; as a noun it is a small gatehouse at the entrance to a country estate.

clue.text: Structural feature of churches I start to contemplate

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the pipe organ is a fixture of most churches
taken as written
the opening letter of contemplate

explanation.surface: Pondering an architectural detail of church buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Structural feature' reads as one phrase about architecture; the definition is the single word 'Structural'.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic can mean inherent in the fundamental constitution of a thing, so relating to its basic structure.

clue.text: Liverpool losing poor first half dismally

indicators.note: losing says some letters are taken out of the city's name
something done dismally is done badly, so the remaining letters are put into a poor order

blocks.note: the city, taken as written
the first two of the four letters of poor

explanation.surface: A football report: Liverpool lost after a dismal, poor first half.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking PO out of LIVERPOOL leaves LIVEROL, which rearranges to ORVILLE. Orville was the green duckling puppet of ventriloquist Keith Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: Orville, a nappy-wearing green duckling who could not fly, was the puppet of British ventriloquist Keith Harris.

clue.text: Elite runners shamefully emigrate after missing opening parts of athletics tournament

indicators.note: acting shamefully means behaving out of line, so the letters are put out of order
missing says some letters are left out of the word before it
the opening part of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of athletics
the first letter of tournament

explanation.surface: Star athletes disgracefully defect, skipping the start of a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests sprinters, but here it means those who run a country. A and T come out of EMIGRATE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is the ruling government of a country, the small elite group of people who run it.

clue.text: 21 down cannot possibly be heard

indicators.note: what can be heard is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: if something cannot possibly be so, it is so in no sense

explanation.surface: A claim that a puzzle answer is beyond hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: the answer to 21 down, naivety.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety and innocence are synonyms, both meaning a lack of worldly experience or guile.

clue.text: Rest of old wine gets drunk

indicators.note: someone drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The dregs of a vintage bottle get finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest of' looks like 'what remains of', but 'Rest' is a verb-phrase definition and 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a short rest is to recline on a bed or sofa for a while, often a nap.

clue.text: Stripped smart car at yard  being joined together — just messing about!

indicators.note: stripped means with the outer layer removed, so the end letters go and the middle is kept

blocks.note: a Cadillac is a smart car; its first two and last two letters are removed
yd is the abbreviation for yard
allying is joining together in alliance

explanation.surface: A car is broken for parts in a scrapyard, while someone fools about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart car' suggests the tiny Smart brand; it is a luxury Cadillac, with two letters stripped from each end.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilly-dally is to waste time through indecision or idling, so doing it is fooling about.

clue.text: Received praise for Rachel's new look

indicators.note: received here means taken in by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound
giving something a new look rearranges it, so those letters are reordered

blocks.note: to laud is to praise; in a British accent with no sounded R the two words are said alike
the fodder, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Rachel's makeover earned her compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the definition: Lord Charles was the monocled dummy of ventriloquist Ray Alan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Charles, an upper-class drunken toff with a monocle, was the famous puppet of British ventriloquist Ray Alan.

clue.text: Almost ready for the table, joining the fish?

blocks.note: first meaning: losing consciousness under anaesthetic, nearly ready for the operating table
second meaning: sinking beneath the waves, down where the fish swim

explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' and 'fish' set up a dinner; the table is in an operating theatre and the fish are in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a patient slipping into anaesthesia before surgery and also a ship or person sinking below water.

clue.text: Mug made of crude copper taking a very long time

blocks.note: pig is a crude, insulting slang word for a police officer
an eon is an immeasurably long period

explanation.surface: A cup made from unrefined metal takes ages to produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude copper' suggests unrefined metal (pig is also a casting of crude metal), but copper is a police officer, and crude marks rude slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a gullible person easily cheated, a dupe who is readily taken in by a swindle.

clue.text: Hit with blow from the side of the hand involves the start of bleeding

indicators.note: to involve is to take inside, so the pair of words wraps round one letter
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
the opening letter of bleeding

blocks.clueFragment: blow from the side of the hand
blocks.note: a karate chop is struck with the edge of the hand

explanation.surface: A martial-arts blow lands and draws blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the definition: Lamb Chop was the sock-puppet lamb of American ventriloquist Shari Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb Chop, a sock puppet sheep, was the famous partner of American ventriloquist and children's entertainer Shari Lewis.

clue.text: What to wear to finish convention

blocks.note: to dress stone or timber is to give it a smooth final finish
a code is a set of accepted conventions

explanation.surface: Deciding on an outfit for the closing day of a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convention' suggests a conference; it means an accepted rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress code is a set of rules telling people which clothes are acceptable for an event or workplace.

clue.text: Steward seen to clash with new order

indicators.note: a new order means the letters are arranged differently from how they stand

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A household manager is seen arguing over new rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A seneschal was the chief steward who ran a medieval noble household and its estates.

clue.text: At home French donkey is asinine

blocks.note: someone at home is in
âne is French for donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey at home in France behaves like a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on asinine, which literally means donkey-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine and inane both mean extremely silly or foolish, lacking sense or meaning.

clue.text: Nylon line gets tangled around some itinerant herons

indicators.note: a tangled line is knotted out of its neat order, so those letters get jumbled
around says the jumbled letters wrap themselves about the other piece

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
some of these words: the last letter of itinerant and the first two of herons, read across the gap

explanation.surface: A fishing line made of nylon gets snagged on some wandering herons.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters split in two to hold the short piece. The preamble supplies the definition: Lenny the Lion was the puppet of ventriloquist Terry Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenny the Lion was the lion puppet worked by the British ventriloquist Terry Hall on 1950s and 1960s television.

clue.text: Our name fails to gain entrance

indicators.note: something that fails breaks down, so the letters collapse into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: We are turned away at the door because our name is not on the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' is not a way in but the verb en-TRANCE, to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to fill them with delight, and to enamour is to make them fall in love.

clue.text: Angel lies about having godlike attributes

indicators.note: about here means round and about, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angel tells untruths regarding divine powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Omniscience, seeing and knowing everything, is a power traditionally ascribed to God, so the word describes a deity-like quality.

clue.text: Firm to stop the flow

blocks.note: first meaning: loyal and committed, unwavering
second meaning: to check the flow of blood from a wound

explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective the word means steadfast; as a verb (also spelt stanch) it means stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch supporter is steadfast and loyal, while staunching a wound means stemming its bleeding.

clue.text: 7 in a foreign check point

indicators.note: foreign means strange and unfamiliar, so the two short words are made strange by rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
to vet is to check thoroughly
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: A checkpoint in some foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference to 7 down, innocence. The answer is itself a French borrowing, often written naïveté.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is lack of experience and worldly wisdom, the same unspoilt quality as innocence.

clue.text: Suspect more by stage one

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful and not to be trusted as it stands, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatrical aside: suspect more on stage one.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the earliest stage of development of an organism, so it represents the first phase of growth.

clue.text: It can come after Michaelmas time of year

blocks.note: the Michaelmas daisy is an autumn-flowering aster
a month of the year

explanation.surface: A riddle about what follows Michaelmas, the autumn feast day of 29 September.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the calendar, but Michaelmas is the first word of a flower name. The preamble supplies the definition: Daisy May was the doll of ventriloquist Saveen.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy May was the little-girl dummy used by the British ventriloquist Saveen on radio and stage in the 1950s.

clue.text: Bush's former presidential familiar has back trouble

indicators.note: back sends the word for trouble going the other way, read right to left

blocks.note: Abe is the familiar short form for Abraham Lincoln, a past US president
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: George W. Bush's predecessor's pet suffers from back pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' with a capital wants to be the president; it is a plant, and the capital is just the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Abelia is a genus of flowering shrubs in the honeysuckle family, grown in gardens for their bell-shaped blossoms.

clue.text: Mistake not to introduce troublesome child

indicators.note: without its introduction means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a little terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: It would be a blunder to bring along a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR loses its T. 'Not to introduce' reads as advice, but it means drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, something done incorrectly through a lapse of judgement or accuracy.

clue.text: Clan gets rich on proceeds from water in the Highlands

indicators.note: what proceeds from something is produced out of it, so the answer is made from these letters rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan grows wealthy from selling water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like money earned; it is the verb, signalling what comes out of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Crinan is a sea loch in Argyll on Scotland's west coast, at the western end of the Crinan Canal.

clue.text: Inlet loses initial smell

indicators.note: losing the initial means the word's opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a creek is a narrow inlet on a coast

explanation.surface: A tidal inlet gives off a bad odour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to give off a strong, unpleasant odour, and as a noun it is that stench.

clue.text: Formerly drab writer cut

indicators.note: a cut name is trimmed, losing its final letter

blocks.note: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: A once-dull author has been edited down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drab' reads as dull; here it is an old noun for a slovenly woman, and 'Formerly' marks the archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English a drab and a trollop were both words for a slatternly or promiscuous woman.
